thread:
maria: Heads-up — seeing a bunch of partial JSON parse errors in the Node SSE client when the host path goes into brief backpressure. Happens when the server pauses ~100-300ms and then resumes, splitting objects across chunks. Example log: \n```\nError: Unexpected end of JSON input
 at JSON.parse (<anonymous>)
 at parseChunk (/src/stream-reader.js:45:12)
```
I've got a tiny repro but wanted to check if anyone's seen this pattern and whether we should prefer NDJSON framing or make the incremental parser more permissive.

devon: Can you paste the read loop? Is this the fetch/ReadableStream approach or EventSource?

maria: fetch + window.ReadableStream in our SDK (node-fetch/polyfill for tests). Read loop basically: 
```
const reader = res.body.getReader()
let buf = ''
while(true){
  const {done, value} = await reader.read()
  if(done) break
  buf += decoder.decode(value, {stream: true})
  // try parse complete json messages from buf
  const endIdx = buf.lastIndexOf('}\n')  // naive
  if(endIdx > -1){
    const chunk = buf.slice(0, endIdx+2)
    buf = buf.slice(endIdx+2)
    handle(JSON.parse(chunk))
  }
}
```
Problem: pauses cause a single JSON object to be split, and our naive boundary detection fails. Also saw some cases where tokens are split in the middle of multibyte unicode sequences and decoder.decode(..., {stream:true}) returns partial chars.

kevin: Yep — we saw similar in the Go client a while back. Two issues to watch: 1) framing strategy (ndjson + explicit \n separator is safest), 2) TextDecoder stream + incremental JSON parsing for JS. For multibyte you need to keep the leftover bytes not-yet-decodable. The browser TextDecoder handles that with {fatal:false} but Node's Buffer-based decode can chop.

sophie: For browser SDK we switched to a small incremental json parser that tolerates partial tokens; it accumulates until a `}` that matches stack depth 0. For Node we used `string_decoder` to preserve utf8 boundaries — avoids mojibake.

devon: Two practical options:
- server side: send ndjson (one JSON per line) or SSE `data: ` frames so client's frame parsing is guaranteed.
- client side: switch to a robust incremental parser (tiny state machine) + keep leftover bytes for decoder.
Which route do we want for short term?

maria: Short term: prefer client fix (less infra churn). I can try swapping to StringDecoder and a stack-depth matcher. Long term we should encourage NDJSON for new endpoints.

kevin: Agreed. Also add backpressure metrics so we can correlate pauses to split-chunks. Please add a histogram of chunk inter-arrival times (ms) in the runtime.

maria: Working on a repro branch now. Quick Q: anyone comfortable reviewing a small parser change in the JS SDK? It's ~80 LOC.

devon: I can review. Ping me with the PR. Link will be helpful in thread.

maria: PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/js-sdk/pull/894 — contains StringDecoder usage + simple brace-matching incremental parser. Test included that reproduces the 200ms pause repro.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary rollout for gateway v1.12.3 started at 2071112270 — 25% traffic. Observability: no 5xx increase in first 60s.

kevin: I'll wire the chunk-timing histogram to the console dashboard so we can see the pause spikes. Assigning to @kevin for telemetry work.

maria: TY — will add the repro steps to the PR description and a small fixture. @devon please tag when ready. :thumbsup:

devon: Will review today. If fine, we'll merge and cut a patch release. Also let's add a short blurb to streaming docs recommending NDJSON or SSE framing when possible.

sophie: I can add the doc note (2 sentences) after the PR merges.
